_comment: PLAT-37 cross-renderer visual parity, macOS. THIS PASS LANDED A FIX and measured it.
The subject is ISONIM-GPUI-ISSUE-E: GPUI ceils every text element's width to a whole
logical pixel, so an editor code row built from one element per coloured span
accumulates that rounding span by span and drifts right of the browser arm.
The remedy landed here draws a declared row as ONE text element carrying per-span
highlight runs, so the width is rounded once per ROW instead of once per SPAN.
THE INSTRUMENT IS THE DRIFT LADDER, NOT P1. The ladder flattened; P1 followed, by less.
Every number below was measured this pass unless marked carriedForward.
standing: HOST-CONDITIONAL EVIDENCE, NEVER A REQUIRED GATE. One macOS host, one display.
measuredThisPass: whetherANEWERgpuiPreDropsTheCeil - every published version 0.3.6..0.3.9 downloaded and grepped
theFixAsLanded - the styled-runs path, its unit tests and its scope
theDriftLadder - pane-level, BEFORE and AFTER, same instrument, both from buffers decoded this pass
parityP1 - all three comparable views, mean/p50/p90/maxError/fracOver0_10
theInterfaceFaceQuestion (PLAT37-ISSUE-G) - OTF vs WEB TTF metrics compared directly
buildOutcomes, freshnessGates, laneOutcomes - both arms rebuilt and recaptured

whetherANEWERgpuiPreDropsTheCeil._question: The brief asked whether bumping the pin would be the cheaper route, since only 0.3.5 was cached locally and this had never been checked.
whetherANEWERgpuiPreDropsTheCeil.answer: NO. The ceil is present and unchanged in EVERY published version.
whetherANEWERgpuiPreDropsTheCeil.method: crates.io sparse index listed the versions; 0.3.6/0.3.7/0.3.8/0.3.9 .crate tarballs were downloaded to a scratch dir (NOT into the cargo registry) and src/elements/text.rs extracted from each.
controls: The same expression WITHOUT .ceil() matched 0 times in every version, so the only form present is the ceiling one.
An absent sentinel string matched 0 times, so the probe is not matching indiscriminately.
0.3.5's and 0.3.9's text.rs differ (diff exit 1) and byte sizes differ (45913 vs 47129 for 0.3.6/0.3.9), so four distinct files really were read.
whetherANEWERgpuiPreDropsTheCeil.recommendation: Do NOT bump the pin for this. It would not help, and tools/check_gpui_pin.sh keeps three copies of the version in agreement with a deliberate '=' - reported as a recommendation, not done.

theFixAsLanded.approach: ONE TEXT ELEMENT PER ROW, via gpui's with_highlights rather than with_runs.
theFixAsLanded.whyWithHighlightsAndNotWithRuns: with_runs requires each TextRun to name a concrete Font. The element builder is a pure function with no Window, and the row's family/size/weight are INHERITED from an ancestor and are only known at layout. with_highlights is resolved against window.text_style() at layout time (gpui-pre/src/elements/text.rs:563-564), so the fused row keeps exactly the face the unfused spans would have used and only the COLOUR is stated by the caller. This is strictly safer than the with_runs route the brief suggested, and needed no new FFI symbol.
theFixAsLanded.noNewAbiSymbol: gpui_ exported symbol count stayed 114 before and after; check_bindings.sh and check_exported_symbols.sh both pass. The work is entirely inside the shim plus one attribute at the call site.

isonimGpuiChanges.rust/gpui-nim-shim/src/render_sync.rs: INLINE_TEXT_RUNS_ATTRIBUTE ('data-inline-text-runs'), struct InlineTextRun{len,color}, fusable_child_text(), inline_text_runs(); GpuiStyles gained PartialEq+Eq (every field is Option<String>).
isonimGpuiChanges.rust/gpui-nim-shim/src/gpui_app.rs: build_plan_div fuses the children when the node declares itself an inline formatting context; new fused_inline_text() maps each span's colour to a HighlightStyle over a byte range. All event, pointer and window-region wiring is reached identically either way.
isonimGpuiChanges.src/isonim_gpui/renderer.nim: inlineTextRunsAttribute, documented, following the windowRegionAttribute precedent.

codetracerChanges.src/frontend/gpui/app/leaves.nim: InlineTextRunsAttribute re-exported, and set on the editor row's CODE span in the highlighted branch only.

theFixAsLanded.safetyRule: A span is fused only if it is text and nothing else: no handler, no window region, and no styling beyond color and flex-shrink. The style test is BY DIFFERENCE FROM THE DEFAULT (clone, blank the two allowed fields, compare to GpuiStyles::default()) rather than by an allow-list, so a property added to GpuiStyles later cannot silently start being fused away - it makes the row fall back instead. Fusing is all-or-nothing per container.
theFixAsLanded.theRenderPlanIsUNCHANGED: The fusion happens in render_plan_to_gpui/build_plan_div, which CONSUME the plan. build_render_plan is untouched, so every token span, its EditorTokenClassAttribute and its colour are still in the plan a test or an introspection reader sees; the code span merely gains one attribute.

unitTests.negativeControl: inline_runs_decline_a_row_that_did_not_declare_itself builds the IDENTICAL row without the attribute and requires None, so the fusing is shown to be driven by the declaration rather than happening to every container.

whatWasDEFERRED.theInlineVALUEchips: The editor's inline-value annotation is a row of CHIPS, each a box with a background, padding and a corner radius, and some carry a 30px 'view more' button with an . Those are real boxes and correctly decline fusion. Within a chip the name and value are text-only siblings and DO still ceil independently.
whatWasDEFERRED.theEvidenceThatThisIsWhatIsLeft: After the fix, editorWithMark has 16 of 21 ladder rows at exactly 0.000% and 5 rows left at 0.95-1.27%; state has 16 of 24 at 0.000% and 8 left. Those residual rows are the ones carrying inline values.
whatWasDEFERRED.theRemedyIfItIsWanted: Declare each chip an inline formatting context and widen the fusable style set to font-weight and font-style, which HighlightStyle already carries as Option<FontWeight>/Option<FontStyle>. Not done here: it is a wider change to the safety rule, and the brief's scope control asks for the editor code rows first.
whatWasDEFERRED.alsoNotDone: ISONIM-GPUI-ISSUE-F (letter-spacing) was informational and was not chased, as instructed.

theDriftLadder._rule: FLIP_DIR has no default and was set explicitly for each reading. BOTH readings were produced by THIS pass with the SAME instrument: the BEFORE buffers are the pre-change captures, copied to flip-before/ before anything was rebuilt, and decoded by the prior pass's compare.sh run; the AFTER buffers were decoded by this pass's compare.sh. The before figures are therefore re-measured here, not quoted.
theDriftLadder.instrument: build/plat37-parity-2026-10-20/advance.py, pane-level column-ink profile, 60 device-px windows, MAXS=6.
theDriftLadder.selfControl: electron-against-electron gave shift 0 in EVERY window of EVERY view, before and after (selfControlNonZeroWindows: 0). A non-zero self shift would have voided the reading.

editorWithMark.reading: The entire monotone ramp is gone. The two early windows (-1 at x=326, +3 at x=356) are unchanged and were never part of the progressive ladder - they are a fixed local feature at the gutter/mark boundary, flat before and flat after.

theDriftLadder.correlationImproved: The tail windows' match improved where the ramp was removed, e.g. editorWithMark x=536 went 0.943 -> 0.995 and x=566 0.962 -> 0.990.

thePerRowLadder.instrument: bandladder.py, the same search restricted to one text band at a time, only for bands whose two arms start within 3 px.

calltrace.note: the least improved view; its editor pane carries proportionally more inline-value chips, which are not fused

thePerRowLadder.theDiscreteSlopesAreGONE: Before, the per-row slopes took the discrete values 0.000/0.278/0.833/1.071/1.290/1.667 that the diagnosis predicted from an integer number of spans per row. After, the modal value is exactly 0.000 and the survivors cluster at 0.95-1.27 - consistent with a residue in rows whose chips still ceil, not with a per-glyph advance difference.

parityP1._rule: CROP_PX=58 was derived from THIS pass's own capture records (titleBarPoints 29 x pointPixelScale 2.0, read from build/plat37-macos/*.capture.json), not inherited.
parityP1.command: CROP_PX=58 ./compare.sh state calltrace editorWithMark editor eventLog shell, in build/plat37-parity-2026-10-20
parityP1.didItMove: YES, and in the right direction, on all three views: state 0.18450347 -> 0.18253356, calltrace 0.19026775 -> 0.18897242, editorWithMark 0.17921914 -> 0.17696894. The mean fell 0.18466345 -> 0.18282497, a drop of 0.00183848 (about 1.0% of the metric).
parityP1.honestReadingOfTheSize: The ladder flattened almost completely while P1 moved only ~1%. That is the expected shape rather than a disappointment: P1 counts every pixel whose FLIP error exceeds 0.10, and the sub-pixel horizontal placement the ceil was corrupting is one contributor among several (antialiasing differences, the interface-face rasteriser, and the residual chip rows all still contribute). The ladder is the specific instrument for the specific defect; P1 is the aggregate. Both moved the right way, and NEITHER is claimed to be solved.
parityP1.whyNotComparable: extent mismatch: gpui 3456x2168 (cropped 3456x2110) vs electron 3840x2160 - the GPUI window is clamped by the display on every 'wide' viewport. That is G1, out of scope, and unchanged by this pass.

theInterfaceFaceQuestion.issue: PLAT37-ISSUE-G, drafted by the 2026-10-19 pass: the INTERFACE face is a different FILE on the two arms - the stylesheet loads SpaceGrotesk WEB .ttf, the GPUI front-end registers SpaceGrotesk_OTF/*.otf - and the 'same outlines' claim had never been verified.
theInterfaceFaceQuestion.answer: VERIFIED, AND THERE IS NO LAYOUT DEFECT. The two files agree exactly on the metrics that decide where interface text lands.
theInterfaceFaceQuestion.whyTheDivergenceIsFORCED: src/frontend/gpui/design_fonts.nim:11-16 documents it: the WEB/fonts/*.ttf carry a broken name table whose family is the literal string 'false' (measured with fc-scan). CSS never notices because @font-face assigns the family itself, but a text system reads the family from the file, so GPUI cannot address those files by family at all. This is a deliberate, documented workaround, not an oversight - so there was no one-line resolution change to make.

measurement.method: A minimal sfnt parser read head.unitsPerEm, hhea.numberOfHMetrics, hmtx advances and the format-4 cmap from each file, and compared the advance of each of 73 ASCII characters NORMALISED TO THE EM.
controls: A face against ITSELF: 0 of 73 differing (the probe does not invent differences).
OTF Regular against OTF Bold: 71 of 73 differing, e.g. 'I' 0.243 em vs 0.264 em (the probe CAN see a difference; a uniform 'identical' answer would otherwise be meaningless).

theInterfaceFaceQuestion.theRemainingCaveat: Only HORIZONTAL METRICS were compared - that is what decides glyph positions. The outline curves themselves were not compared, and CFF and glyf can rasterise with slightly different pixel coverage at the same size. The browser also prefers the .woff2 of the same WEB set over the .ttf; the .woff2 was not decoded (no brotli to hand), so this measurement assumes the WEB .ttf and .woff2 are the same font in different containers.
theInterfaceFaceQuestion.recommendation: Close PLAT37-ISSUE-G as 'no layout defect, divergence forced and documented', keeping the rasterisation caveat as the open remainder.

gpuiPlanTest.whyTheFailureIsNOTthisPassSchange: The failing test is 'PLAT-50 GPUI: Files', and the assertion that fired is `ck mr.len > 0` where mr = multiRoot(). multiRoot() (line 82) scans test-logs/tui-fixtures for a directory whose name starts with 'multi_root-'; this host has only calc-2f0db4f45192, so it returns the empty string. The test's own `if mr.len > 0:` guard then skips its remaining 8 assertions, which is exactly the 108-100 shortfall. It is a MISSING FIXTURE on this host, environmental and pre-existing, and has nothing to do with text, spans or fusion.
